Chapter 100: Isn't This a Bit Too Fast?

Guo Feng quickly returned after his shower, having probably skipped the public bathhouse and just used cold water in the utility room.

His hair wasn't even dry.

Guo the Madman completely ignored Bian Guanyue's presence and was eager to talk about work the moment he arrived: "That thing you mentioned about automatically aggregating friends' statuses, photos, relationship changes, and other information, I really can't build it right now. That's why I brought Senior Dong here today, to discuss solutions with him."

"Did you come to a conclusion?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Dong Qianqiu took over: "A dynamic feed needs storage, computing, and algorithms, a complete three-part chain. The technology isn't there yet. Memcached can only help boost performance a little. The GFS paper Google released last year, and the MapReduce paper from this year, are both discussing distributed storage solutions. We might be on the eve of a technological breakthrough."

This was not a problem a small company could solve.

They could only wait for Silicon Valley's technology to upgrade. Another two years or so should be enough, by which time Hadoop 1.0 would be open-source.

Facebook also launched its first modern dynamic feed two years later.

Chen Guiliang asked: "With our current resources, what kind of dynamic interactive features can we create?"

Guo Feng explained:

"Content can only be centered around personal profiles, blogs, and photo albums, with interaction relying on users actively clicking to visit each other. We can add an SMS notification feature to tell a user's friends that they've updated a comment, a photo, and so on."

"Setting up a blog function, forwarding a friend's blog post, recommending alumni from the same city, recommending friends of friends to be added... these features are doable."

Chen Guiliang asked: "Can't we import content from other blog platforms?"

At this time, blogging was the most fashionable and trendy thing to do, and it was extremely difficult to snatch users from Sina Blog.

Guo Feng shook his head: "Let's not even talk about the technical issues. Other blog platforms simply won't open up their data APIs."

"Let's build the features you mentioned first," Chen Guiliang had no choice but to give up on his ahead-of-the-times request. "Once our campus network is out, we'll definitely be able to crush the ChinaRen Alumni Directory in one fell swoop!"

As early as 1999, ChinaRen had launched its Alumni Directory. Its registered users quickly surpassed 4 million, with over 200,000 daily active users, covering 80% of the nation's colleges and universities.

In 2000, Sohu acquired ChinaRen in a stock swap worth 30 million USD.

Up until last year, the Alumni Directory held 90% of the market share for campus social networking in China, with an average daily PV of over 50 million.

So why did Chen Guiliang say the market was wide open, and why did Guo Feng actually believe him?

Because the Alumni Directory was already failing.

Of all the companies acquired by Sohu, which one could escape the fate of decline?

As early as three years ago, the founders of ChinaRen had been forced out of Sohu, and the founding team was directly disbanded.

Sohu defined the Alumni Directory as a traffic-driving tool and absolutely did not allow it to operate independently. After the founding team was dissolved, the thing was even more neglected, like an unwanted stepchild. It went without updates or maintenance for a long time, the user experience was abysmal, and its various features were stuck in the past.

In an era of rapid technological advancement in the internet industry, a social networking platform had actually gone years without adding a single new feature. It was as if time had stood still.

It was nothing but a dying behemoth!

"You guys carry on."

Chen Guiliang gave Bian Guanyue a ride on his bike, quickly reaching the area outside the south gate. He said to the owner of a barbecue stall, "Give me 30 large kidneys, 100 lamb skewers, and just throw in some other random things."

After speaking, he went to a nearby store and bought two dozen cans of beer.

"Are these for them?" Bian Guanyue asked.

Chen Guiliang said, "They're working hard. A little treat to show my appreciation, and I'll have a drink with them."

Bian Guanyue said, "You must be very tired too, right? With so many classes, and running a company."

"My time to be tired hasn't come yet. The promotion phase is when I should be putting in the effort," Chen Guiliang asked with a smile, "How about we hang out for a few more days during the National Day holiday? I can take you around all the nearby schools."

"Mhm," Bian Guanyue replied, lowering her head.

The two chatted while waiting for the barbecue to be done. Chen Guiliang got on his bicycle, hanging the plastic bags of beer on both ends of the handlebars. Bian Guanyue still sat on the back seat, helping to carry the barbecue skewers.

"Ding-a-ling-ling..."

The bicycle rode along the side of the street. Chen Guiliang would ring the bell from time to time to remind pedestrians ahead to be careful.

The lights were brilliant all around, and the streets were bustling with activity.

Bian Guanyue rested the side of her face against Chen Guiliang's back, admiring the beautiful night scenery of the streets, thinking it would be perfect if life could be like this forever.

"I'll sing for you," Bian Guanyue said.

Chen Guiliang smiled, "Okay."

"The amber dusk is like sugar in the beautiful distance, your face wears no makeup but I've madly fallen in love, longing and shadows are stretched long together at nightfall..."

Her style of singing was different from Jay Chou's.

Bian Guanyue's voice was clearer and brighter, her enunciation crisper, carrying a young girl's yearning for love.

Amidst that sweet and clear singing voice, Chen Guiliang's legs pedaled with even more vigor. He only knew a part of the song, and when it got to that part, he joined in: "I'm under the scorching sun, just wanting to hold an umbrella for you, you lean on my shoulder, afraid of forgetting to breathe..."

The bicycle sped along the roadside, happening to pass by an elderly professor couple.

The old couple was out for a walk. Seeing the two approaching from a distance, singing a sweet love song together, smiles instantly bloomed on their wrinkled faces.

The old couple stopped walking and stood there watching, their eyes following them as they rode far away.

"It's great to be young," the old woman said.

The old man said, "Yes, it is."

"Stop working, let's have a late-night snack first."

Chen Guiliang put the two dozen beers on the table, and Bian Guanyue came over with the barbecue skewers.

"Yo, you remembered to report back. Old Dong, come on over and indulge with us," Guo Feng said, swallowing.

Dong Qianqiu also cheered up: "Just one can of beer for me. I still have to work tonight."

Chen Guiliang said, "Work my ass. We'll talk about it tomorrow."

Dong Qianqiu smiled and didn't insist. He thought this Chen Guiliang fellow was a pretty good guy.

Chen Guiliang also opened a can for Bian Guanyue, raised his beer, and said, "Come on, let's have a toast. Senior Dong, I won't feed you some story about a Silicon Valley startup founder becoming a millionaire. You study computer science, so you must be sick of hearing stories like that. Regardless of whether you join the company in the future, we're all friends for being able to get together now!"

"Alright."

Dong Qianqiu pulled the tab on his can, and after clinking them together, he only took a small sip before starting on the lamb skewers.

Guo Feng grabbed a large kidney skewer and started eating.

Bian Guanyue used to be indifferent to social situations and never cared about pleasing anyone.

At this moment, she carefully recalled her father and stepmother's usual words and actions. Seeing Guo Feng take a few bites and then reach for his beer, she said, a bit awkwardly, "Senior Guo, I'd like to toast you. It's a pleasure to meet you. I wish you and Chen Guiliang's company great success and prosperity."

"Thanks."

Guo Feng only had eyes for his senior schoolmate, but Bian Guanyue had still left him somewhat impressed. After clinking cans and drinking, he said to Chen Guiliang, "Your girlfriend is very pretty."

Chen Guiliang smiled, "That senior schoolmate of yours is surely even prettier."

Guo Feng, however, shook his head, "In terms of looks alone, she definitely can't compare to your girlfriend. But my senior... how should I put it? That feeling... well, it's indescribable."

Dong Qianqiu, who hadn't been saying much, couldn't help but laugh out loud while eating his skewers.

"What are you laughing at?" Guo Feng said, annoyed.

Dong Qianqiu said, "I was just remembering your senior's birthday last year. You gave her a bouquet of carnations. You didn't even dare to say anything, you just threw the flowers down and ran, and you even tripped on your way downstairs."

Bian Guanyue said, confused, "Aren't carnations for mothers?"

Guo Feng stressed, "I gave her white carnations. They represent 'my love will last forever,' the purest kind of love, and can also bring good luck to women."

Bian Guanyue said, "But if you like your senior, you could give her roses."

"You don't understand. Roses are too vulgar, not worthy of her," Guo Feng said.

Dong Qianqiu held back his laughter and said nothing.

Chen Guiliang winked at Bian Guanyue.

Bian Guanyue immediately dropped the topic and raised her beer again, "Senior Dong, I'd like to toast you too. I'm very happy you could come and help."

"You're welcome," Dong Qianqiu quickly clinked his can with hers.

The four of them started drinking, eating skewers, and chatting idly. By the time they finished the barbecue, it was almost 11 p.m.

Chen Guiliang urged them to go back to their dorms: "Hurry back and get some sleep. When you wake up tomorrow, your minds will definitely be clearer. Don't ruin your health before the website is even done."

"Why do you sound just like my mom?" Guo Feng grumbled, but he listened to Chen Guiliang's arrangement.

Perhaps it was because of the alcohol, but Dong Qianqiu had become more talkative. He clapped Chen Guiliang on the shoulder and said, "Junior, I think building a website is pretty interesting, and you're a really good guy. But I've already applied for an internship at Microsoft Research Asia. If Microsoft accepts my application, I'll start in December. Before December, I can come here and help. If Microsoft doesn't want me... well, I'll seriously consider your offer."

"Then I wish Senior Dong success in getting into Microsoft. My doors here will always be open," Chen Guiliang said.
